hints.content: In order to find $g'(2)$, we should first find an expression for $g'(x)$ for any input $x$.

Since $f$ and $g$ are inverses, we can use the following identity that holds for any two differentiable inverse functions:

$g'(x)=\dfrac{1}{f'\Bigl(g(x)\Bigr)}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
To use this method, you ***do*** need to remember **the chain rule**:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[v\Bigl(u(x)\Bigr)\right]=v'\Bigl(u(x)\Bigr)\cdot u'(x)$

Since $f$ and $g$ are inverses, we know the following equality holds:

$f\Bigl(g(x)\Bigr)=x$

We can differentiate both sides of the equation according to $x$:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[f\Bigl(g(x)\Bigr)\right]=\dfrac{d}{dx}(x)$

While the right-hand side of the equation is simply $1$, the left-hand side can be evaluated using the chain rule:

$f'\Bigl(g(x)\Bigr)g'(x)=1$

Now we isolate $g'(x)$ and we're done!

$g'(x)=\dfrac{1}{f'\Bigl(g(x)\Bigr)}$
options.showPrompt: Is there a way to memorize this identity?

hints.content:
We can now plug $x=2$ into this expression and evaluate. Here is the table of values again, for your convenience:

$x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | $f'(x)$
:-: | :-: | :-: | :-: 
$2$ | $1$ | $9$ | $\dfrac13$
$9$ | $2$ | $10$ | $\dfrac{1}{12}$

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
g'(2)&=\dfrac{1}{f'\Bigl(g(2)\Bigr)}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{f'(9)}&&\gray{g(2)=9}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{12}}&&\gray{f'(9)=\dfrac{1}{12}}
\\\\
&=12
\end{align}$
